name: l2cap_send_contract
prototype: struct l2cap_stock { u16 total; u16 payload_offset; u16 cid; u16 handle; ...; u8 type; u8 flags; }

ownership.argument: Ownership: the caller allocates and the handler frees, so after bt_l2cap_submit_cid the module must not touch the buffer. Zero-length payload is supported: the handler computes total - payload_offset == 0 and takes its header-only branch.

provenance.source: Measured from both ends. Caller side: allocate with l2cap_stock_alloc 0xC7EAFBC(payload_len, header_len), fill the payload at buf + 4 + payload_offset, then call bt_l2cap_submit_cid 0xC805BE8(buf, cid). That wrapper writes the cid dword at buf+4 (low u16 = cid, high u16 = the caller's second word) and posts a work node {owner, handler 0xC801D10, done 0xC7EBD40, arg = buf, flag 1} through l2cap_work_submit 0xC7EB988. Handler side: reads the same words (+0 total, +2 payload offset, +4 cid/handle), re-fragments in place into 8-byte nodes chained through *(channel+4) using the channel fragment size at +106, writes the four-byte L2CAP header immediately before the payload, sets the flags byte at +10 to 0x81 (first|last) on the single-fragment path, and frees the buffer with bt_free on every exit path.

notes: Ownership: the caller allocates and the handler frees, so after bt_l2cap_submit_cid the module must not touch the buffer. Zero-length payload is supported: the handler computes total - payload_offset == 0 and takes its header-only branch.
